questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.
A government decides to subsidise farms producing milk in its country. Which question about this decision is a normative question rather than a positive question?

options.A: How much will milk production increase?
options.B: How should essential products, such as milk, be produced?
options.C: How will employment in the milk industry change?

questions.questionText: Economy X uses its resources in the labour-intensive production of wheat and wooden furniture as shown by the production possibility curve FW. With the help of new strains of wheat seeds, X increased yields and shifted to a new production possibility curve. Which diagram depicts this change?

options.A: B furniture furniture F F O W O W wheat wheat
options.C: D furniture furniture F F O W O W wheat wheat

questions.questionText: What is most likely to severely affect the ability of money to act as a medium of exchange?

options.A: a devaluation of a country’s rate of exchange for foreign currency
options.B: an increase in the money supply
options.C: a very high rate of inflation
options.D: a very high rate of interest

questions.questionText: What would not affect the position of the demand curve for wigs?

options.A: an increase in incomes
options.B: a reduction in the price of hairdressing
options.C: an increase in wigs worn by television celebrities
options.D: a reduction in the price of wigs

questions.questionText: In which situation is the demand for a product said to be price elastic?

options.A: The quantity demanded responds to a change in price.
options.B: An increase in price brings about a decrease in the quantity demanded.
options.C: An increase in price induces consumers to spend more on the product.
options.D: A decrease in price brings about an increase in revenue.

questions.questionText: In the diagram D D is a straight line demand curve and D D is a rectangular hyperbola curve.

Over a four year period, as the price of new houses increases, the price elasticity of supply for new houses falls, as shown. All new houses were sold. supply of new price of new price elasticity houses houses ($) of supply year 1 10000 100000 – year 2 10250 110000 0.25 year 3 10450 125000 0.13 year 4 10600 140000 0.12 What shows price elasticity of supply became more inelastic from year to year?

options.A: Dollar revenues to house builders declined each year.
options.B: Each year, the government released more land for house building.
options.C: The proportionate price change was greater than the proportionate supply change.
options.D: The proportionate price change was the same as the proportionate supply change.

questions.questionText: Prices of gold, silver and copper fell considerably in 2011 and again in 2015. The fall in 2011 was said to be because miners increased production. The fall in 2015 was because demand, especially from China, decreased. Assuming that the equilibrium before 2011 was X, how would these movements in 2011 and subsequently in 2015 be shown on the demand and supply diagram? price X T Q S R O quantity initial 2011 2015 equilibrium equilibrium equilibrium

options.A: X Q R
options.C: X S R

questions.questionText: Consumer X is the largest of five consumers and buys 50% of sales. The table shows the quantity of the good demanded by consumer X and the market supply of the good. price demand from market supply $ consumer X
What does not happen when price acts as a means to allocate resources?

options.A: Price determines the supply of public goods.
options.B: Price operates in the markets for both goods and factors of production.
options.C: Price recognises consumers’ ability to pay rather than consumers’ needs.
options.D: Price signals to producers which goods are most profitable.

questions.questionText: What is meant by consumer surplus?

options.A: the amount of money that remains after consumers have made their purchases
options.B: the difference between how much a consumer is willing to pay for a good and the amount paid
options.C: the difference between the amount of a good that’s bought by a consumer and the amount consumed
options.D: the difference between the price paid for a good and the cost of producing it

questions.questionText: In the diagram, S is the original supply curve and D is the original demand curve. S W price S V T R P Q D O M N quantity If supply shifts to S , which area represents the change in consumer surplus?

options.A: PQVT B PQW C PRVT D TVW

questions.questionText: After a series of poor harvests, a government imposes an effective maximum price on cereals. What would be a consequence of this policy?

options.A: Both rich and poor people would satisfy their demands equally.
options.B: Illegal buying and selling through a black market would be prevented.
options.C: Rationing would be necessary to ensure a fair distribution of cereals.
options.D: The market would fail to clear leaving a surplus of cereals.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the demand and supply curves of a commodity before and after a specific tax is removed. S S price
The diagram shows the market for heating oil. S price D O quantity If the government introduces a production subsidy, how will the financial benefit be shared between consumers and producers?

options.A: It will be shared equally between producer and consumer.
options.B: It will go entirely to the producer.
options.C: The majority will go to the consumer.
options.D: The majority will go to the producer.

questions.questionText: The diagrams show UK Government total spending and welfare spending in £ billions between 2005 and 2014.

Health services in an economy are provided by private clinics that charge high fees. The government decides health services should be provided for everyone, not based on ability to pay. Which direct action should it take?

options.A: Build government clinics to compete in the market.
options.B: Close private clinics where provision by the market is inadequate.
options.C: Increase the taxes on profits made by private clinics.
options.D: Nationalise private clinics and remove charging.

questions.questionText: In its recent budget a government reduced total expenditure while increasing the amount spent on training to increase the productivity of the workforce. The initial equilibrium point is shown by X on the aggregate demand (AD) and aggregate supply (AS) diagram. What would be the equilibrium point after these changes? AS AS price level C AS X B D A AD AD AD

The table shows the retail prices index for four countries for years 2 and 3. (Year 1 index = 100 for all countries.) Which country had a higher rate of inflation in year 2 than year 3? country year 2 index year 3 index
What does the current account of the balance of payments include?

options.A: government reserves and foreign aid
options.C: imports and exports of goods and services
options.D: inflows and outflows of trade and capital

questions.questionText: Assume the Chinese monetary authorities are committed to maintaining the exchange rate of China’s currency, the Yuan, against the US$ between P and P on the diagram.
In the UK in July 2014, £1 = US $1.71. By the end of August 2014, £1 = US $1.65. What is most likely to explain this?

options.A: an increase in UK exports
options.B: an increase in UK interest rates
options.C: increasing profitability of UK companies
options.D: increasing size of UK national debt

questions.questionText: Which formula is used to calculate a country’s terms of trade?

options.A: index of export prices − index of import prices
options.B: index of import prices – index of export prices index of export prices
options.C: × 100 index of import prices index of import prices

questions.questionText: Country X forms a customs union with country Y. X then ceases to produce its own cars and instead imports cars from Y. Country Y diverts some of its car exports to X from country Z. How is this likely to affect car prices in X and Z? country X country Z

options.A: decrease decrease
options.C: increase decrease

questions.questionText: The table shows the ability of two countries to produce two commodities when they use all of their resources for that product. maximum output maximum output country of rice of wheat X 2000 2000 Y 4000 2000 Which statement is correct?

options.A: Country X has an absolute advantage in wheat.
options.B: Country Y has an absolute advantage in wheat.
options.C: Country X has a comparative advantage in wheat.
options.D: Country Y has a comparative advantage in wheat.

questions.questionText: In 2014, Poland was the world’s largest exporter of apples. 55% of the crop went to Russia. Then Russia banned the imports. What would not have prevented the revenue of the Polish apple farmers falling dramatically?

options.A: The apple farmers found new markets in other countries.
options.B: The apple farmers were able to store the harvest for sale later.
options.C: The Polish Government placed a ban on imports of food from Russia.
options.D: The Polish Government established a scheme to buy apples and supply them to charities.

questions.questionText: Monetary policy can be used to increase the level of business activity. Which action illustrates this?

options.A: curbing consumption through controls on credit
options.B: lowering reserve requirements of banks to increase lending
options.C: reducing government spending to achieve a budget surplus
options.D: stimulating company investments by increasing interest rates

questions.questionText: When will a country’s balance of payments current account deficit be reduced?

options.A: when it lowers tariffs on its imports
options.B: when it raises its rate of income tax
options.C: when it removes export subsidies
